script: OpenAI just gave ChatGPT a tiny coworker with its own computer — and it doesn’t clock out. They’re called Dots. Instead of living inside one chat bubble, a Dot can connect to your apps, use its own cloud computer, and keep chewing through a multi-step job in the background. OpenAI is pitching them for real work and personal errands, with specialist Dots for companies, and teams of Dots planned later. But here’s the catch: sensitive actions can still need your approval, and right now Dots require an eligible paid ChatGPT plan, while Meta’s Muse offers a free tier. So the next AI race isn’t just who has the smartest chatbot. It’s who gets to become your always-on digital coworker. Would you give one the keys?
audience: AI-curious adults and knowledge workers deciding whether persistent agents deserve access to their apps
rationale: Derivation precedes staging. Propositions and semantic verbs: [0,20) introduce, equip, persist, name; [20,39) leave containment, connect, operate separately; [39,49) advance successive assigned steps behind another activity; [49,70) apply, distinguish present uses from preview specialists and future teams; [70,81) interrupt sensitive execution and await a person; [81,98) compare access conditions; [98,119) reframe competition from answering to sustained participation; [119,125) offer access while preserving the person's decision. Adjacent propositions share a setup only while their spatial rule evolves. Containment becomes connection; connection resets to sequential progress; progress resets to a present/future folio; permission resets to an access comparison; comparison resets to a change of working relationship. A small conceptual Dot token carries identity across these worlds. The opening and closing share access imagery, but the ending leaves access physically withheld. All described assets, targets and action contracts are intended production contracts, not assertions of existing implementation.
metaphor: A small paper Dot moves between distinct tactile software worlds: a separate computer, connected app sockets, an advancing assignment ribbon, a present-and-future folio, a permission latch, access ledges and a working relationship. No single room contains all these mechanisms.

limitations: DATA-ONLY PLAN. No tools, files, web, external reference film, artwork, speech generation, animation or critic execution were used. Structure and direction are NOT_ASSESSED; this plan does not grant approval.
Verified facts are restricted to the supplied source packet. Interfaces are conceptual illustrations. Continuous motion signifies persistence, not measured runtime, speed or guaranteed completion.

Agent-assisted production-scoped SVG additions requested: dot-token, cloud-desk, route-dock, job-fold, preview-folio, permission-latch, access-ledges and coworker-shift. Their SVG and JSON metadata paths are intended contracts. No canonical promotion is requested.

Agent-assisted action adapters requested only after structure approval: dots-cloud-seat-v1, dots-route-connect-v1, dots-ribbon-advance-v1, dots-folio-reveal-v1, dots-permission-stop-v1, dots-access-compare-v1, dots-workplane-shift-v1 and dots-human-key-offer-v1. The requested: prefix means unavailable pending development, not a registered action kind.

Each adapter must develop the explicitly named anchor contracts, expose actual focus targets and bind them to approved framing. Asset IDs here are logical intended targets, not invented DOM selectors. Missing target or anchor resolution blocks compilation.

Contact development must resolve token seats, connector/socket alignment, ribbon feeds and stops, folio hinges, slip/shutter stops, pedestal landing and human hand/key attachment. The human key grip requires inverse attachment resolution after the authored hand and key transforms. Any local contact deformation or residual response must be explicitly implemented and reviewed within the requested adapter; none is assumed to execute through current reaction bindings.

Reuse the canonical puppet, existing tactile materials, approved fonts, event engine, paper captions and lexical voice alignment. Their existing resource locations must be resolved from the production registry; no unprovided resource paths are invented in this plan.

Bot appears only in the opening setup. Its performance and sole numeric reaction use the registered interactive-ui-v1 bot target. No screen, token, keyboard or pointer reactions are claimed. Other reaction target arrays are empty until explicit adapters expose approved bindings.

Calendar/arena, paper and workshop finite actions do not already execute these Dots worlds. Their unrelated plots are not substituted. Workshop worker targets and unsupported whole-body/gripped-tool reactions are not used.

PREVIEW specialist and PLANNED team markings are persistent local artwork, independent of narration captions. The specialist is veiled; the team fold remains unopened with empty slots. No operating team is shown.

Eligibility and gradual rollout remain qualified. Dots is not shown as exclusive to a $100 plan; Muse is not shown as unlimited or equal in capabilities. Sensitive actions remain pending; background examples are read, organize and draft work.

Actual Kokoro timing at the supplied voice speed drives duration. Action cues remain verbatim within their beat narration. Caption chunks follow real lexical alignment and do not dictate setup resets.

The independent structure critic must pass before direction review, speech and moving rough. Both independent moving critics must assess all required gates with and without captions before final artwork; final moving QA repeats before audio finishing. No pass is claimed.

Moving contact evidence requires consecutive native six-frame windows before and after each meaningful declared event, clipped at beat boundaries, plus moving traces. Event scheduling must remain within the evidence system's eight-event per-shot bound without imposing a creative quota.

At most two meaningful moving repair rounds are authorized by the brief. Technical checks and final human watching/listening approval remain separate requirements. The system never publishes or grants approval.
